title: PepsiCo to Cut About 1,000 North America Jobs in Restructuring
excerpt: North America CEO Ram Krishnan told staff the changes, due within a week, will simplify a structure he called complex and fragmented, after beverage volumes fell 2% last quarter.
body:
• PepsiCo is eliminating about 1,000 jobs across its North American food and beverage operations over the coming week, a restructuring first reported by The Wall Street Journal.
  • North America CEO Ram Krishnan told staff in a November 9 memo that "too much of how we work today remains complex and fragmented" and that changes will clarify accountability and speed decisions.
  • The cuts follow a weak third quarter in the home market: North American beverage volumes fell 2%, food volumes were flat, and management cut its full-year core EPS growth outlook to 1% to 2%.
  • PepsiCo employed about 306,000 people worldwide at the end of last year, including about 125,000 in the United States.

PepsiCo Inc. is eliminating about 1,000 roles in North America as it seeks to simplify its organisational structure, Bloomberg reported, with the maker of Mountain Dew and Doritos acting after a weaker earnings outlook and a warning from management that the region's recovery is taking longer than expected, according to Reuters.

"Too much of how we work today remains complex and fragmented."

— Ram Krishnan, CEO, PepsiCo North America

Ram Krishnan, the company's North America chief executive, sent a November 9 memo to workers saying PepsiCo has opportunities "to simplify our structures, clarify accountability and make decisions faster," and that "over the coming week, we'll make changes across parts of our organisation to address this." The Wall Street Journal reported the job cuts earlier on November 9. Reuters said PepsiCo had not immediately responded to its request for comment, and no specific savings target for the 1,000 positions has been disclosed.

The numbers behind the decision

PepsiCo's October 8 earnings release showed third-quarter revenue of $25.274 billion, up 5.6%, with organic revenue growth of 3.1%. Underneath that growth, the home market stalled: North American beverage volumes fell 2% and food volumes were flat, and the company's core operating margin contracted 35 basis points to 16.9%. CFO Steve Schmitt said on the earnings call that price cuts and marketing investment were taking longer than expected to lift sales. PepsiCo has also struggled to hold market share for its salty snacks following price increases, and recently lost its contract with KFC's US restaurants to Coca-Cola, Bloomberg reported.

Management has already lowered its full-year core constant-currency earnings-per-share growth forecast to 1% to 2%, from the low end of a 4% to 6% range, and now expects approximately 3% organic revenue growth. Chief executive Ramon Laguarta said further structural cost reductions would fund growth initiatives and help offset rising input costs. The restructuring was already carrying a cost before this round: PepsiCo recorded $185 million of charges under its existing productivity plan in the 12 weeks ended September 5, up from $141 million a year earlier, its quarterly filing shows.

What to watch next

The cuts are expected to be carried out within about a week and span the North American food and drinks businesses. What investors will look for next is whether PepsiCo quantifies the restructuring — the savings target and any charge — in its next earnings communication, and whether a simpler structure revives the beverage volumes that price cuts and marketing have so far failed to move. Read the Bloomberg report via Transport Topics and the Reuters-based analysis at MarketSpeaker.
